customSections.label: Calendar Notes for Military-Connected Families
customSections.content:
Cumberland County Schools serves a large military-connected community near Fort Bragg. Families arriving during the school year should first confirm which CCS calendar applies to their school: the district publishes separate Traditional, Year-Round, Cross Creek and Cumberland International, and Cumberland Polytechnic calendars. Opening dates and breaks differ among those files.

CCS provides transition resources through its Military Connection program and district Military Family and Youth Liaisons. For enrollment, school assignment, IEP, 504, transfer, or Interstate Compact questions, contact CCS directly. Those issues fall outside the scope of this calendar page. The calendar dates here should not be used as a substitute for enrollment or student-services guidance.

calendarFaqs.q: When does Cumberland County Schools start and end in 2026–27?
calendarFaqs.a: Traditional-calendar students start Monday, August 24, 2026. The last student day is Friday, May 28, 2027, with a two-hour early release.

calendarFaqs.q: Does every CCS school use the Traditional Calendar?
calendarFaqs.a: No. CCS also publishes separate Year-Round, Cross Creek and Cumberland International, and Cumberland Polytechnic calendars. Confirm the calendar assigned to your school or program.

calendarFaqs.q: When are the major CCS student breaks?
calendarFaqs.a: Traditional-calendar students are out for Thanksgiving Week on November 23–27, 2026; Winter Break on December 21, 2026–January 1, 2027; and the spring no-school period on March 25–April 2, 2027. These are planning labels; CCS uses several official calendar categories within each period.

calendarFaqs.q: Does CCS officially call March 25–April 2 Spring Break?
calendarFaqs.a: No. The Traditional Calendar divides those consecutive student no-school dates among a workday, district holiday, annual-leave days, and a telework workday. This page calls it a spring no-school period for planning clarity and explains the official categories in the date list.

calendarFaqs.q: Does CCS have early-release days in 2026–27?
calendarFaqs.a: Yes. Traditional-calendar students are released two hours early on September 22, October 20, December 18, February 23, March 9, April 20, and May 28, the last day of school.

calendarFaqs.q: Is February 15, 2027 a regular no-school day?
calendarFaqs.a: It is listed as a student holiday and required staff workday, but CCS also reserves February 15 as a make-up day if needed. Check district updates before making plans.

calendarFaqs.q: Where is the official CCS 2026–27 calendar PDF?
calendarFaqs.a: Use the Official PDF link on this page or open the CCS board-approved calendars page. The official page also provides the Year-Round, early-college, and Cumberland Polytechnic calendars.

calendarFaqs.q: Does the downloadable calendar update automatically?
calendarFaqs.a: No. The ICS file is a one-time import and will not update automatically if CCS revises a date or activates February 15 as a make-up day.

sourceReviewSummary: Reviewed August 8, 2026, against the current CCS board-approved calendars page, the linked Traditional Calendar PDF, and the district's 2026–27 back-to-school guide.
sourceReviewDetails: The current Traditional Calendar marks August 24 as the first student day and May 28 as the last student day with a two-hour early release.
November 23–27 and March 25–April 2 are editorially grouped as student no-school periods. The PDF uses several workday, holiday, annual-leave, and telework labels within those ranges.
February 15 is both a student holiday/required workday and the calendar's listed make-up day if needed.

The district calendar page labels the current files as board approved July 1, 2026, while the PDF headers display earlier approval stamps. This page uses the dates in the files currently linked by CCS and records that source-label mismatch rather than resolving it by inference.
The 2026–27 back-to-school guide confirms July 16 for Year-Round students, August 10 for the two early-college schools and Cumberland Polytechnic, and August 24 for Traditional students.
